resolvedQuestions.text: Per skill, which routing mechanisms exist, where is one routing decision restated, and where have the copies drifted?
Which mechanisms make each of the five routing decisions in sk-code, sk-doc, sk-design and system-deep-loop, and where is each decision restated?
Where have restated copies of the same routing decision drifted, and which copy is authoritative?
Which checks, parsers, templates, generators, benchmarks and runtime mirrors enforce the current routing shape, and what would each proposed change break?
Should hubs, mode packets and standalone skills each use a per-mode ROUTER.md, one hub ROUTER.md, the advisor hybrid, or JSON-only?
Which checks, parsers, templates, generators, benchmarks and runtime mirrors enforce the current shape, and what would each proposed change break?
Which readability problems does each skill show, and which quoted passages demonstrate them?
Which routing shape wins for hubs, for mode packets and for standalone skills: per-mode ROUTER.md, one hub ROUTER.md, the advisor hybrid, or JSON-only?
What phased implementation plan, with order, risk and rollback, follows from the evidence?
What readability defects exist per skill, with quoted passages?
What phased implementation plan (order, risk, rollback) delivers the winning shape?

keyFindings.text: `cli-external-orchestration` restates executor vocabulary in four separate machine-readable places: `mode-registry.json` aliases (12/5/6/5/6/9/8 phrases per mode at lines 37, 74, 104, 135, 165, 196, 230), `hub-router.json` `vocabularyClasses` (13/7/7/5/9/10/9 alias keywords plus a dispatch class, from line 104), `ROUTER.md` `INTENT_SIGNALS` (10/11/11/10/11/9/10 keywords, line 93), and each packet's `<!-- Keywords: -->` comment (for example `cli-devin/SKILL.md:8`). A read-only set comparison found 6 registry aliases missing from `ROUTER.md` for `cli-opencode` (for example "parallel opencode session", "in-opencode parallel session") and 8 `ROUTER.md` keywords missing from the registry for `cli-devin` (for example "swe-2 dispatch", "devin cloud session"). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/hub-router.json:104] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/mode-registry.json:37] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/ROUTER.md:93]

**sk-code restates stage-one mode selection in four live places plus one generated artifact.** The registry is named the source of truth at `SKILL.md:54`; the same selection is re-expressed as Python `route()` at `SKILL.md:76-134`; as weighted classes in `hub-router.json:24-39`; as a 40-line prompt-keyword row in `ROUTER.md:252` (CI_WORKFLOW); and as the compiled projection `.skilled/bin/compiled-route.cjs` invoked at `SKILL.md:56-60`. `mode-registry.json` itself carries only 4 modes, with 83 aliases across them (13 quality, 10 review, 5 skilled, 55 ci). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/SKILL.md:54] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/hub-router.json:21]

**ROUTER.md §2 and §9 have drifted in both directions, not one.** The report's claim that §2 lists TESTING (`ROUTER.md:57`) and LANGUAGE_STANDARDS (`ROUTER.md:60`) with "no §9 key" is confirmed: §9 `INTENT_SIGNALS` runs `IMPLEMENTATION, CODE_QUALITY, DEBUGGING, VERIFICATION, HOOKS, CONFIG, JAVASCRIPT, TYPESCRIPT, PYTHON, SHELL, RUST, CI_WORKFLOW` (`ROUTER.md:241-252`). The report missed the converse: five §9 intents — JAVASCRIPT, TYPESCRIPT, PYTHON, SHELL, RUST — have no §2 prose row at all, so the "byte-for-byte source" claim at `ROUTER.md:223` holds for neither direction. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/ROUTER.md:241]

Stage-two leaf routing has three disagreeing definitions per mode. `ROUTER.md` says every mode's first slice is `references/cli-reference.md` plus `references/integration-patterns.md` (lines 103-132). `cli-devin/SKILL.md` says the ALWAYS slice is `references/cli-reference.md` plus `assets/prompt-quality-card.md` (line 86) while its `RESOURCE_MAP` sends GENERATION to `references/cli-reference.md` plus `assets/prompt-templates.md` (line 112). `cli-hermes/SKILL.md` repeats the same split (ALWAYS at line 93, `RESOURCE_MAP` at line 117). Three documents, three answers to "what loads first". [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/ROUTER.md:103] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-devin/SKILL.md:86] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-hermes/SKILL.md:93]

All seven mode packets carry a complete Python router (`INTENT_SIGNALS`, `RESOURCE_MAP`, `LOADING_LEVELS`, `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST`) and restate the same six-step call sequence; only the helper bodies are shared. `cli-devin/SKILL.md:92-148` is representative: the dictionaries are inline and the call sequence is six numbered steps. The shared reference those packets point at still describes "the six cli-* sibling skills" and lists six providers, omitting `cli-hermes`, which defers to it at `cli-hermes/SKILL.md:101`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/cli/shared-smart-router.md:17] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/cli/shared-smart-router.md:139] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-hermes/SKILL.md:101]

**Three docs each claim a different routing authority.** `SKILL.md:54` says "`mode-registry.json` is the single source of truth"; `sk-code-review/SKILL.md:612` says "Keep Section 2 (`SMART ROUTING`) as the authoritative routing source"; `ROUTER.md:223` calls its §9 block "the byte-for-byte source a deterministic router parses". Only the third is measurably true — `parseRouter` reads the §9 block — so the other two are restatements that contradict the parser. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-review/SKILL.md:612] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/ROUTER.md:223]

`cli-classifier` restates the Jev vocabulary four times and its hub router contradicts the packet's own baseline. `mode-registry.json` has 9 aliases (line 36); `hub-router.json` has a 9-keyword `cli-jev-aliases` class and a 17-keyword `jev-dispatch` class (lines 24, 37); `ROUTER.md` has four intent lists of 10/8/7/4 keywords (line 58); `cli-jev/SKILL.md` repeats them again in `INTENT_MODEL` (line 117). The hub router declares `DEFAULT_RESOURCE = []` and "no hub-wide preamble" (`ROUTER.md:51-54`), while the packet declares `DEFAULT_RESOURCES` with two always-loaded files (`cli-jev/SKILL.md:115`) — the same routing decision, two incompatible statements. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-classifier/hub-router.json:24] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-classifier/ROUTER.md:54] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-classifier/cli-jev/SKILL.md:115]

**The CI vocabulary is copied five times with three different sizes.** `hub-router.json:76-78` `code-ci-aliases` (55 keywords), `ROUTER.md:252` CI_WORKFLOW (61 keywords), `sk-code-ci/SKILL.md:62` (12 keywords), `mode-registry.json` `sk-code-ci.aliases` (55), plus the packet's `RESOURCE_MAP` at `sk-code-ci/SKILL.md:65`. The hub-router class and the registry alias list happen to agree today; the ROUTER.md row and the packet row do not, and the packet's own header admits the divergence is deliberate ("Every keyword is multi-word, so a bare 'workflow' never scores this surface", `sk-code-ci/SKILL.md:56`). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/hub-router.json:76] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-ci/SKILL.md:62]

The advisor's stage-one input duplicates the same phrases a fifth time. `cli-external-orchestration/graph-metadata.json` holds 73 `intent_signals` (line 63) and 87 `derived.trigger_phrases` (line 139); `description.json` adds its own keyword list (line 6); `cli-classifier/graph-metadata.json` holds 33 `intent_signals` (line 32) drawn from the same Jev phrases as the router. A phrase added to one list does not propagate to the others, and the comparison in finding 1 shows the drift already exists. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/graph-metadata.json:63] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/graph-metadata.json:139] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-classifier/graph-metadata.json:32]

**The report's own inventory numbers are off and must be corrected before a plan quotes them.** It says `mode-registry.json`, "about 59 aliases"; the actual count is 83. It cites `hub-router.json:77` as a CI-vocabulary copy — line 77 is the `code-ci-aliases` keyword array, so the anchor is right but it is one class, not the class list. The direction of its conclusion survives; its quantities do not. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/mode-registry.json:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/hub-router.json:77]

The enforcement surface that reads `ROUTER.md` is the leaf manifest, not the benchmark. `leaf-manifest.json` enumerates `modes[].leaves` from the packets, so a `RESOURCE_MAP` path must resolve and be registered; `ROUTER.md` itself says the block is what "the deterministic router-replay parses" (line 48). The benchmark claim in `SKILL.md:76` ("the deterministic router-replay and benchmarks parse") is stale: `benchmark/README.md` states the Lane C harness, runner and scoring contract were removed and no new run can start. The prose advertises an enforcement that no longer runs. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/leaf-manifest.json:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/ROUTER.md:48] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/benchmark/README.md:20]

**Two packets advertise routing the tooling does not read.** `sk-code-quality/SKILL.md:30` carries a 15-term "Keyword triggers:" line and `sk-code-quality/SKILL.md:154-156` calls the deterministic router-replay "retired", while `sk-code-skilled/SKILL.md:178` documents that same replay as the live leg-1..4 guard. One of the two statements is stale; the guard is the one that runs. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/SKILL.md:154] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/SKILL.md:178]

Readability: routing prose comes before the instructions in both hubs and is written in long compound sentences. `cli-external-orchestration/SKILL.md` has 27 lines over 200 characters, the longest 779 characters at line 76: "Stage 2 of routing lives in `ROUTER.md` at the hub root, next to `SKILL.md` and `README.md`. It defines the per-mode leaf-intent model (every mode in `mode-registry.json`, plus the deliberate absence: a bare CLI-dispatch phrase that names no executor fires no intent and defers at the hub), the machine-readable `DEFAULT_RESOURCE` / `INTENT_SIGNALS` / `RESOURCE_MAP` block that the deterministic router-replay and benchmarks parse, and the how-to-read rules (dominant intent → one leaf set; near-tied intents → deduped union, the `orderedBundle` outcome; no keyword match → hub `defer`, never a silent default to `cli-opencode`)." `cli-devin/SKILL.md` has 47 lines over 200 characters, the longest 1,397 at line 333, a single numbered rule carrying a persona-injection contract, a roster path, a fallback mechanism and an exceptions clause. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/SKILL.md:76] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-devin/SKILL.md:333]

**Stage-two leaf choice has no runtime script, so the leaf map is model-only.** `compiled-route.cjs` emits packets (`hub-router.json:24-39` `resources: ["<packet>/SKILL.md"]`), and `leaf-manifest.json` is a generated, checked artifact with no router consumer — its readers are tests and the compiler (`compiled-route-admission.cjs`, `parent-skill-check-leaf-manifest.test.cjs`). So D4 (which leaf files) is decided by prose and by each packet's own machine block, never by a resolver. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/hub-router.json:24] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/leaf-manifest.json:1]

**Readability: routing precedes instructions and jargon precedes definition.** In `sk-code-review/SKILL.md` the SMART ROUTING section opens at line 49 and the first executable step block opens at line 67; the report's 364-line/50% measurement is consistent with the section boundaries I read. The opening sentence of `sk-code-quality/SKILL.md:15` reads verbatim: "`quality` is the author-side quality gate MODE child of the `sk-code` family. It runs after the acting agent applying `workflow-implement.md` changes the code and before the surface's verification workflow or done-claim." The hub's own opening is a four-metaphor sentence: "One skill, two axes, one shared surface-detection router, and one advisor identity." (`SKILL.md:15`). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/SKILL.md:15] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/SKILL.md:15]

Stage one can route to `mcp-obsidian` on signals stage two has no leaf set for. `mode-registry.json` gives `mcp-obsidian` 26 aliases (line 265), including the health, Iconic rulebook, Excalidraw and Minimal-theme families; `hub-router.json` wires those families into the `mcp-obsidian` signal through four classes (line 56). `ROUTER.md`'s `OBSIDIAN` intent has 13 keywords (line 97), none of which is health, iconic, excalidraw or theme. A request that scores on those classes selects the mode, then matches no stage-two intent and defers. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-tooling/mode-registry.json:265] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-tooling/hub-router.json:56] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-tooling/ROUTER.md:97]

**Two hubs assign opposite authorities to the same stage-one vocabulary.** sk-doc says "each nested packet's single `Keyword triggers:` line is the source of truth for its routing vocabulary; `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json` are synchronized projections" (`sk-doc/SKILL.md:53`); sk-code says "`mode-registry.json` is the single source of truth" (`sk-code/SKILL.md:54`). Whichever wins, one hub's model is wrong today. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/SKILL.md:53] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/SKILL.md:54]

**Nothing parses the declared source of truth.** A search of every `.cjs/.js/.ts/.py/.mjs` under `.skilled` and `.pi` for `Keyword triggers` returns zero code hits. The machine reader, `router-replay-lib.cjs`, resolves a hub's modes from `hub-router.json` and its leaves from `ROUTER.md`; the `Keyword triggers:` line is prose only. So sk-doc's "source of truth" is a convention enforced by review, not by a check. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/SKILL.md:53] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/assets/scripts/router-replay-lib.cjs:1]

The mcp hub repeats the same four-list vocabulary pattern and the same drift, measured the same way: registry aliases (6/6/26/7/14/7/6/6/6 at lines 52, 86, 120, 158, 195, 231, 265, 319, 363), `hub-router.json` vocabulary classes (23 classes from line 23), `ROUTER.md` `INTENT_SIGNALS` (11/11/13/11/14/11/8/9/6 keywords from line 94), and each packet's `<!-- Keywords: -->` comment. Comparing registry aliases with `ROUTER.md` found 6 `mcp-chrome-devtools` registry phrases absent from the router, 5 `mcp-click-up`, 6 `mcp-obsidian`, 4 `mcp-aside-devtools`, 1 `mcp-notion`, 4 `mcp-figma`, 2 `mcp-refero` and 4 `mcp-mobbin`; only `mcp-magicpath` matched exactly. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-tooling/mode-registry.json:52] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-tooling/hub-router.json:23] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-tooling/ROUTER.md:94]

**The "synchronized projection" claim is false today.** Comparing the 173 backticked terms across the 14 packets' `Keyword triggers:` lines with the union of `hub-router.json` vocabulary keywords finds 17 terms absent from the projection. `sk-create-diff` is the worst: 5 of its 7 triggers — `document before/after review`, `before/after document diff`, `review document edits`, `docx diff`, `pdf diff` — exist nowhere in `hub-router.json`. Every `/create:*` and `/doc:quality` slash form is also absent (for example `/create:readme`, `/create:skill-parent`). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-diff/SKILL.md:30] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/hub-router.json:1]

Unlike the CLI hub, the mcp packets state the same fallback contract the hub router states. Every packet declares `DEFAULT_RESOURCE` plus `DEFAULT_RESOURCE_SEMANTICS = "fallback-only"` (for example `mcp-obsidian/SKILL.md:152-156`, `mcp-figma/SKILL.md:122-124`), and the hub router declares `DEFAULT_RESOURCE = []` with "No always-loaded preamble" (`ROUTER.md:90-92`). The wording is restated ten times, but the semantics agree: the default is a defer-time suggestion, never unioned into a scored route. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-obsidian/SKILL.md:152] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-figma/SKILL.md:122] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-tooling/ROUTER.md:90]

`mcp-code-mode` is the working model for a standalone skill: no `mode-registry.json`, no hub router, and still a typed leaf projection. Its SKILL.md says so directly — "mcp-code-mode is a normal, standalone single-mode skill whose sole workflow mode is `mcp-code-mode` (there is no `mode-registry.json`)" — and it ships `leaf-manifest.json`, `leaf-manifest.config.json` and `leaf-aliases.json`, regenerated with `generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --write`. The generator lives at `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/generate-leaf-manifest.cjs`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-code-mode/SKILL.md:62] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-code-mode/leaf-manifest.config.json:7]

**Stage two is hub-owned in sk-doc and packet-owned in sk-code, on the same decision.** Only 5 of 14 sk-doc packets carry a `RESOURCE_MAP` machine block (`sk-create-benchmark:115`, `sk-create-frontmatter:80`, `sk-create-repo-rule:89`, `sk-create-skill:106`, `sk-create-with-human-voice:89`); the other 9 have no router block and depend entirely on `ROUTER.md` §3, which names every packet's leaves packet-qualified. sk-code does the reverse: all four packets carry blocks and the hub block duplicates them. Both shapes pass the same checks today, which matters for the verdict — one hub already demonstrates that per-mode blocks are optional. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/ROUTER.md:145] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-readme/SKILL.md:42]

`mcp-code-mode`'s router declares a default that cannot act as one. `DEFAULT_RESOURCE = "references/workflows.md"` (line 74) is also the only `LOADING_LEVELS["ALWAYS"]` entry (line 103), and the fallback `if not loaded: load_if_available(DEFAULT_RESOURCE)` (lines 195-196) therefore runs only when the ALWAYS file is missing. The "default" is an always-load, so the fallback branch is dead in normal operation. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-code-mode/SKILL.md:74] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-code-mode/SKILL.md:103] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-code-mode/SKILL.md:195]

**sk-doc forbids the hub-level move the report proposes to test, by name and mechanism.** `SKILL.md:65` states the machine block "must not move into `SKILL.md` (the replay would treat it as the hub's own router and lose the mode projection) or into `hub-router.json` (schema handoff-ambiguity rule)". That is a hub-level constraint, not a packet-level one: no document forbids moving a packet's own block inside its own `SKILL.md`, which is where the block already lives. The report's plan is safe at packet level and blocked at hub level, and the two cases were conflated. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/SKILL.md:65]

**The JSON cost grows with the mode count, and so does the drift surface.** sk-doc spends 605 lines of `mode-registry.json` and 477 of `hub-router.json` for 15 modes and 152 aliases — 40 registry lines per mode; sk-code spends 130 and 83 for 4 modes and 83 aliases — 33 lines per mode. The per-mode cost is roughly constant, so the alias drift in finding 3 is a function of mode count, not of the hub. A shape that keeps one JSON per hub must budget for that growth or generate it. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/mode-registry.json:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/hub-router.json:1]

The same regeneration instruction is actionable in one skill and unactionable in the other. `mcp-code-mode` names the exact command and the byte-stability check (`SKILL.md:62`); `mcp-tooling` says only "Regenerate `leaf-manifest.json` through the canonical metadata command" (`SKILL.md:126`) without naming the command, the script or the check. An operator reading the hub cannot perform the instruction from the text. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-tooling/SKILL.md:126] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-code-mode/SKILL.md:62]

Readability splits sharply between the two skills. `mcp-tooling/SKILL.md` is the cleanest hub read so far: 152 lines, 8 lines over 200 characters, and a 17-line §2 (lines 48-64) that states the two stages before any table. `mcp-code-mode/SKILL.md` puts 155 lines of §2 before its first instruction, 134 of them a Python block, and line 62 is a 972-character paragraph: "**Typed leaf projection (fleet routing standard).** mcp-code-mode is a normal, standalone single-mode skill whose sole workflow mode is `mcp-code-mode` (there is no `mode-registry.json`). Every routable leaf under `references/`, `assets/`, and the manual-testing playbook is enumerated in `leaf-manifest.json`, generated from `leaf-manifest.config.json` (regenerate with `generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --write .skilled/skills/mcp-code-mode`; it must stay byte-stable under `--check`)." [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-tooling/SKILL.md:48] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/mcp-code-mode/SKILL.md:62]

**Readability: the routing definition is a 107-word run-on, and the trigger lines are ungrouped term dumps.** `sk-doc/SKILL.md:53` reads verbatim: "Routing is **registry-driven at runtime and packet-authored at source** in two stages. Stage 1 (hub → mode): each nested packet's single `Keyword triggers:` line is the source of truth for its routing vocabulary; `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json` are synchronized projections that the hub reads without re-deriving mappings during a request. The advisor routes any documentation/authoring query to the single identity `sk-doc`; the hub then picks the packet. Stage 2 (mode → leaves): the root `ROUTER.md` maps the request's authoring intent to the exact packet-local leaf resources that mode loads. The two layers stay separate: the hub never emits leaf paths, and the surface router never re-decides the mode." The frontmatter packet's trigger line (`sk-create-frontmatter/SKILL.md:36`) is 28 terms with no grouping, mixing field names, error symptoms and version formats. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/SKILL.md:53] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/SKILL.md:36]

**Hub shape already diverges inside the same skill family.** sk-doc carries `leaf-aliases.json` (5 alias entries) and `leaf-scopes.json` in addition to `leaf-manifest.json`; sk-code carries only `leaf-manifest.json`. `leaf-aliases.json` is read by `router-replay-lib.cjs` and `parent-skill-check.cjs`, so the extra file changes which paths a guard can resolve — the hubs are not interchangeable inputs to the same checks. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/leaf-aliases.json:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/leaf-manifest.json:1]

All four roots are Class S by the fleet contract, not by convention: a Class S root declares neither `mode-registry.json` nor `hub-router.json`, and `description.json`, `mode-registry.json`, `hub-router.json` and `command-metadata.json` are **forbidden** for S while `leaf-manifest.config.json` is required and `leaf-manifest.json` plus `leaf-aliases.json` are generated. The contract names exactly these roots: "**S** (7) | `cli-orca`, `mcp-code-mode`, `sk-git`, `sk-prompt`, `sk-vision`, `system-skill-advisor`, `system-spec-kit`". `sk-vision/SKILL.md:66` restates it: "No `mode-registry.json`, no `hub-router.json`, no `description.json`." [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/references/shared/skill-root-metadata-contract.md:41] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/references/shared/skill-root-metadata-contract.md:54] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-vision/SKILL.md:66]

**The rule that blocks the hub-level move is copied in four hubs, and one copy has drifted.** sk-doc `SKILL.md:65`, system-deep-loop `SKILL.md:50` and cli-external-orchestration `SKILL.md:78` carry the sentence verbatim, including "(schema handoff-ambiguity rule)"; sk-design `SKILL.md:74` paraphrases it as "nor into `hub-router.json`, which is a different schema". The rule is the single most load-bearing constraint on the restructuring question, and its justification is now paraphrased in one of the four places that state it. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/SKILL.md:65] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-design/SKILL.md:74]

**Hub-level only: no document extends the forbid to a packet's own `SKILL.md`.** Every copy of the rule names "the machine block" moving into *the hub's* `SKILL.md` or into `hub-router.json`. Since a packet's machine block already lives in the packet's own `SKILL.md`, moving it within that file is outside the rule's wording. The advisor report conflated the two cases; the texts do not. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/SKILL.md:50]

`sk-vision`'s router cannot route. It declares one intent (`VISION`, line 84), maps that intent to two directory prefixes (`feature-catalog/`, `manual-testing-playbook/`, line 97-99), and `route_resources` loads every markdown file under both prefixes whenever the inventory is non-empty (lines 130-142). `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` returns only when the corpus is empty, never for an unrecognised request. The `INTENT_SIGNALS` keywords are therefore decorative: any invocation loads the whole corpus. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-vision/SKILL.md:84] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-vision/SKILL.md:97] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-vision/SKILL.md:130]

`cli-orca` declares weights its router never reads and carries a unique ownership map. Every intent declares `"weight"` (lines 102-110), but lane selection at line 177 is `max(INTENT_SIGNALS, key=lambda name: sum(signal in signals for signal in INTENT_SIGNALS[name]["keywords"]))` — a count of matched phrases, not a weighted score. ruledOutDirections.text: Counting "keyword triggers" lines as a routing decision: the CLI packets have none; their triggers live in the `<!-- Keywords: -->` comment, which no parser in this iteration was found to read.

Treating `benchmark/reports/**` as live enforcement. The reports are frozen archives from an older worktree and the harness is retired (`benchmark/README.md:20`), so they are evidence of past behaviour only.

Treating the mode packets' `INTENT_SIGNALS` as a duplicate of the hub's. They encode a different decision (task intent inside one executor), so the duplicate is the leaf mapping, not the intent names.
Treating the mcp hub as a copy of the CLI hub. Its stage-two contract is consistent with its packets, so the CLI drift is a packet-level defect, not a universal hub defect.
Treating `DEFAULT_RESOURCE = []` and `DEFAULT_RESOURCE = "references/x.md"` as a contradiction. Both declare fallback-only semantics; the difference is representation.
Searching the mcp packets for a per-mode `ROUTER.md`: none exists. Every packet routes from its own SKILL.md block.
A per-mode `ROUTER.md` for standalone skills. Class S forbids the hub files outright, so the option is not available, not merely inadvisable.
Treating the four standalone routers as interchangeable. Their scoring implementations differ; only `sk-git` handles word boundaries.
Looking for `description.json` in the standalone roots: the contract forbids it, and none exists.
Counting `.hermes/skills` against `find .skilled/skills -name SKILL.md` without excluding `node_modules`: the three extra hits are Playwright's bundled skills, correctly not mirrored.
Treating all five phrase lists as live routing sources. Only `graph-metadata.json` feeds stage one; the rest are documentation or dead metadata.
Treating the Hermes mirror as a text copy of routing prose that can be hand-edited. It is generated and `--check` enforces it.
Treating ROUTER.md as removable on the strength of the CLI hub's duplication alone. `router-reach` reads it and fails without it.
Treating the hypothesis report as confirmed wholesale. Its hub and standalone conclusions hold; its "remove the per-packet loading tables" needs the correction in finding 2.
Trying to express stage-two leaf choice in today's JSON without a script. The compiled router emits packets, not leaves (prior report), and no leaf resolver exists for hub routes.
Deleting the packet task-intent maps. They answer a different question from the hub's executor map.
Pure JSON-only routing for hubs. `router-reach` reads `ROUTER.md` as stage-two vocabulary.
A per-mode `ROUTER.md` for any class. Class S forbids the hub files; Class H's router is hub-root only; no packet carries one.
